result.note: A personal milestone with little policy content; one question tests the distinction between continuous and total tenure records.

questions.prompt: In June 2026, Narendra Modi completed 4,399 consecutive days as Prime Minister. Consider the following statements:
items: With this milestone, Modi became India's longest-serving Prime Minister by total tenure.
Modi has held office without interruption since May 2014, winning general elections in 2014, 2019 and 2024.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because Jawaharlal Nehru, who governed from 1947 until his death in 1964, remains the longest-serving Prime Minister by total tenure. Modi's record is for the longest continuous stint as an elected Prime Minister, counted from the first general election.
questions.source: Jawaharlal Nehru remains India's longest-serving Prime Minister by total tenure, having governed from 1947 until his death in 1964.
